title: Super Micro contractor pleads guilty in scheme to divert AI servers with Nvidia chips to China
source_used: Reuters (text read on the WTVB copy)
key_facts: Ting-Wei "Willy" Sun, a contractor linked to Super Micro Computer, pleaded guilty in a scheme to illegally export servers containing advanced Nvidia AI chips to China, per a court filing reported on Friday 9 Oct 2026.
The court docket showed Sun entered the plea on Thursday 8 Oct in US District Court in Manhattan.

In March, prosecutors charged Sun and two others associated with Super Micro, including a co-founder, with conspiring to divert about $2.5 billion of US AI technology to China in violation of export laws.
The alleged scheme began around 2024 and used a company in Southeast Asia as a pass-through to conceal the China-based end customers, per the indictment.
Nvidia B200, H100 and H200 GPUs and servers containing them are on the Commerce Control List.
Super Micro did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment; its shares were down marginally in extended trading.
quote_evidence: A contractor linked to Super Micro Computer has pleaded guilty in a scheme to illegally export computer servers containing advanced Nvidia AI chips to China, according to a court filing on Friday.
The court docket showed Sun entered his guilty plea on Thursday in U.S. District Court in Manhattan.
The alleged scheme began around 2024, with the defendants accused of using a company in Southeast Asia as a pass-through entity to conceal the China-based end customers, according to the indictment.
